 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO a) CALL FOR THE ENTIRE RECORDS LEADING TO PASSING OF THE ORDER DATED 09.08.2023 IN APPLICATION No.10779/2022 PASSED BY THE LEARNED KARNATAKA STATE ADMINISTRATIVE TRIBUNAL, BELAGAVI AND SET ASIDE THE IMPUGNED ORDER DATED 09.08.2023 (ANNEXURE-A)
AND ETC.
 THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B'
GROUP, THIS DAY THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1. We have heard the learned counsel appearing on either sides. 
2. We have also perused the common judgments in Writ Petition No.10050/2021 and connected matters. 
3. In view of the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner that the issue raised before this Court in the said common judgment as well as in this writ petition are identical,
We had requested the learned Government Advocate to get instructions in the matter. 
4. It is submitted by the learned Government Advocate that the matter is gaining attention of the Government in terms of the common judgment and that some time is required for consideration of the matter and that atleast three months NC: 2024:KHC:19451-DB time may be required by the Government to take a final decision in the matter. It is stated that the writ petition can be disposed of in the same fashion as in the connected judgment and that liberty may be given to the Government as has been granted in the said matter as well.
5. Having considered the contentions advanced and in view of the fact that the petitioner had been working as Food Safety Officer from the year 2011 and since, he has been further promoted and has thereafter retired from service in the year 2022, We are of the opinion that the finding that he is not entitled to salary attached to the post of Food Safety Officer cannot be accepted. We therefore dispose of the writ petition in the same fashion as has been done in the common judgment. 
ORDER (i) The Writ Petition is partly allowed.
(ii) The orders of the Tribunal rendered in Application No.10779/2022 dated 09.08.2023 passed by the Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal is set-aside. 
Sri H B Shivakumar vs The State Of Karnataka on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116326266/
2 NC: 2024:KHC:19451-DB (iii) Respondents shall consider the application as a representation and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law and consequently, pay the applicant such Salary as attached to the post of Food Safety Officer.
6. It is made clear that despite the discussion made herein above and in view of the fact that no prayer for declaration of appointment having been sought, the observations with regard to the appointments are clarified as not conclusive and it is open for the respondents to take such action as is permissible under law, in the event, respondents come to the conscious decision that the applicant is not appointed to the post of Food Safety Officer in accordance with the FSS Act within a period of three months and the consequential relief shall be released to the petitioner at the earliest at any rate within an outer period of one month thereafter.
